steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the 'fs' (file system), 'path', and 'http' modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. For example: const fs = require('fs');
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have three require statements importing the fs, path, and http modules.
successCriteria: fs, path, and http modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Node.js modules needed for file serving.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but need all three: fs, path, and http.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the module names and syntax. Use require() to import 'fs', 'path', and 'http'.

steps.title: Create the main server function
steps.instruction: Define a function called 'createSecureFileServer' that takes a port number as a parameter.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should accept one parameter (e.g., port).
steps.seedCode:
// Import required modules here

// Define createSecureFileServer function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createSecureFileServer is defined with a port parameter.
successCriteria: The createSecureFileServer function is defined and accepts a port parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the main server function with the correct parameter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the function is named exactly 'createSecureFileServer' and accepts a port parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Please define a function named 'createSecureFileServer' that takes a port parameter.

steps.title: Initialize server configuration
steps.instruction: Inside the createSecureFileServer function, create a variable named 'baseDir' to store the base directory path (use './public') and another variable named 'allowedExtensions' as an array containing allowed file extensions: '.html', '.css', '.js', '.png'.
steps.hint: Use const to declare both variables. For allowedExtensions, create an array literal with the four string values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function now contains two configuration variables: baseDir with the public directory path and allowedExtensions with the four allowed file extensions.
successCriteria: The createSecureFileServer function contains a 'baseDir' variable set to './public' and an 'allowedExtensions' array with '.html', '.css', '.js', '.png'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the server configuration variables. The base directory and allowed extensions are now defined.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some configuration, but make sure you have both variables: 'baseDir' with './public' and 'allowedExtensions' as an array with all four file extensions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration variables aren't set up correctly. Inside the function, create 'baseDir' with './public' and 'allowedExtensions' as an array containing '.html', '.css', '.js', '.png'.

steps.title: Create the request handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the createSecureFileServer function, define a function named handleRequest that takes request and response objects as parameters.
steps.hint: Add a function declaration with two parameters, typically named req and res.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRequest function is defined inside createSecureFileServer, ready to process incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A function named handleRequest is defined with two parameters (request and response objects).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the request handler function. This will be the core of your server's request processing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named handleRequest with two parameters inside createSecureFileServer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleRequest function isn't properly defined. Check that it's inside createSecureFileServer and has two parameters.

steps.title: Parse and sanitize the requested URL path
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, parse the URL from the request object and use path.normalize() to sanitize the requested file path.
steps.hint: You can get the URL from req.url, then use path.normalize() to clean up the path and prevent directory traversal attacks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRequest function now includes code to parse the URL and sanitize the path using path.normalize().
successCriteria: The handleRequest function contains req.url parsing and path.normalize() call to sanitize the file path.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully parsed the URL and used path.normalize() to sanitize the file path, which helps prevent directory traversal attacks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using both req.url to get the URL and path.normalize() to sanitize it within the handleRequest function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. You need to parse the URL from the request object and use path.normalize() to sanitize the file path inside the handleRequest function.

steps.title: Validate file extension
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, after parsing the URL path, check if the requested file's extension is in an allowed extensions array.
steps.hint: You can create an array of allowed extensions (like ['.html', '.css', '.js', '.png']) and use the path.extname() method to get the file extension from the sanitized path.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRequest function will include logic to validate the file extension against a list of allowed extensions.
successCriteria: The code includes an allowedExtensions array and checks if the sanitized path's extension is in that array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added file extension validation to prevent serving unsafe file types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking the extension against an array of allowed extensions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file extension validation is missing or incorrect. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Check if file exists
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, after validating the file extension, use fs.existsSync() to check if the sanitized file path exists on the filesystem. Store the result in a variable named fileExists.
steps.hint: Call fs.existsSync() with the sanitized path as the argument. The result will be a boolean (true if the file exists, false otherwise).
steps.analogousExample:
// Checking if a file exists
const fileExists = fs.existsSync(filePath);
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRequest function now includes a file existence check using fs.existsSync(), with the result stored in a fileExists variable.
successCriteria: The code uses fs.existsSync() to check file existence and stores the result in a variable named fileExists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the file existence check. This is a crucial security step before serving any file.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fs.existsSync() correctly and storing the result in a variable named fileExists.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file existence check is missing or incorrect. Use fs.existsSync() with the sanitized path and store the boolean result in a fileExists variable.

steps.title: Serve the file or return 404
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, after the file existence check, add an if-else statement: if the file exists and has a valid extension, create a read stream with fs.createReadStream() and pipe it to the response with the appropriate Content-Type header; otherwise, return a 404 status with a 'File not found' message.
steps.hint: Use the fs module's createReadStream method to stream the file content. Set the Content-Type header based on the file extension before piping. For 404, use res.writeHead(404) and res.end().
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now properly serve valid static files with correct MIME types or return a 404 error for invalid requests.
successCriteria: The handleRequest function includes an if-else statement that uses fs.createReadStream() to serve valid files with Content-Type header, and returns 404 for invalid requests.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the core file serving logic. The server now correctly handles valid file requests and returns appropriate errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you include both the file serving branch (with createReadStream and Content-Type) and the 404 branch?
steps.feedbackWrong: The file serving logic is missing or incorrect. Review the example: you need an if-else statement that either serves the file with proper headers or returns 404.

steps.title: Create and start the HTTP server
steps.instruction: Inside the createSecureFileServer function, create an HTTP server using http.createServer() with your handleRequest function as the request handler, then call server.listen() to start it on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use http.createServer(handleRequest) to create the server, then call server.listen(3000) to start listening.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createSecureFileServer function now creates and starts an HTTP server that uses your secure file serving logic.
successCriteria: An HTTP server is created with http.createServer(handleRequest) and started with server.listen(3000) inside the createSecureFileServer function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created and started the HTTP server that will use your secure file serving handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're creating the server with http.createServer(handleRequest) and starting it with server.listen(3000).
steps.feedbackWrong: The server creation or startup is missing or incorrect. You need to create the server with http.createServer(handleRequest) and start it with server.listen(3000).

steps.title: Export the server function
steps.instruction: Export the createSecureFileServer function using module.exports to make it available for use in other modules.
steps.hint: Add a module.exports statement at the end of your file, assigning the function to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createSecureFileServer function is exported and can be imported and used in other Node.js modules.
successCriteria: The createSecureFileServer function is exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the server function, making it available for use in other modules.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're exporting the function correctly using module.exports.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't exported yet. Use module.exports to export the createSecureFileServer function.
